authors: Zifan Zhang;Pei Wang;Xiuchen Wu;Wen Zhang;Yang Li;Renjie Guo;Xiaona Wang;Zekai Meng
title: Hot drought reshapes the relationship between tree species diversity and forest resilience
abstract: Climate warming is increasing the occurrence of hot droughts, in which water deficits coincide with anomalously high temperatures, posing growing risks to forest ecosystems and carbon sequestration. Yet whether tree species diversity (TSD) affects forest resilience differently under drought-only and hot drought remains unclear. Here, we conducted a global assessment of TSD effects on NDVI-based forest resilience following drought-only and hot drought events. By integrating satellite-based estimates of resilience with global tree species richness data and environmental factors across ten major forest biomes, we found that global forests exhibited reduced post-drought growth under both drought conditions, with more spatially extensive reductions under hot drought. Importantly, the TSD-resilience relationship differed markedly between the two drought types. TSD effects on forest resilience were widely negative under drought-only conditions but were predominantly positive under hot drought. Hot drought also amplified both positive and negative TSD effects relative to drought-only events. Interaction analyses further showed that, under drought-only conditions, TSD effects were broadly modulated by mean annual temperature and vapor pressure deficit, whereas under hot drought, mean annual temperature was the only environmental variable showing widespread modulation of TSD effects. In addition, resilience was more sensitive to the number of tree species under hot drought and in species-poor forests. Our findings highlight that anomalously high temperature accompanying drought reshapes both the direction and magnitude of TSD effects on forest resilience and identify low-richness regions as strategic targets where management interventions may deliver greater ecological benefits.

explanation: 该论文研究了2025年欧洲极端热浪的成因，重点关注大气环流和人为强迫对高温条件的影响。虽然未直接提及遥感技术，但其涉及大气成分分析（温度异常）、气候变化归因等与遥感技术密切相关的研究内容，因此判定为强相关。
authors: Yan Chen;Wen Chen;Shangfeng Chen;Juan Feng;Tianjiao Ma
title: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
abstract: In summer 2025, an extreme heatwave propagated northeastward across Europe, sequentially affecting Southwestern (SWEU) and Northern (NEU) Europe with record-breaking durations in the 1979–2025 record. However, the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the 2025 European high-temperature conditions remain unclear. Here we show that atmospheric circulation explains 82.5% (95% uncertainty interval: 65.0%–99.0%) and 51.9% (37.0%–65.2%) of the regional mean maximum temperature (Tmax) anomalies averaged over the respective heatwave periods in SWEU and NEU, respectively, based on the flow analogue method. Extreme anticyclonic circulation is associated with extreme Arctic Oscillation and British–Baikal Corridor (BBC) patterns in SWEU, and BBC and Atlantic–Eurasia patterns in NEU. Detection and attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 simulations show that anthropogenic forcing increases the probability of exceeding the European mean June-July Tmax level observed in 2025 by a factor of 194.0 (95% confidence interval: 128.3–298.6). Greenhouse gas forcing increases the likelihood of exceeding this threshold, whereas anthropogenic aerosol forcing reduces it. These results provide insights into the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in European high-temperature conditions.

explanation: 该论文使用多时相和多传感器的遥感技术来制作咖啡分布图，并评估其对欧盟防森林砍伐法规的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是卫星观测和土地利用变化分析。
authors: Tin W Satriawan;Xiangzhong Luo;Shafira Nur Ramdhania;Agustín Escobar-López;Anggun Tridawati
title: Nearly ninety percent of Indonesian coffee area is classified as deforestation-free under the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)
abstract: Indonesia is the third-largest coffee producer globally and exports a substantial share of its production to European Union (EU) countries. Recent implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which requires deforestation-free supply chains, highlights the need for spatially-explicit coffee mapping to support the assessment of coffee-associated deforestation. In this study, we utilized multitemporal and multi-sensor remote sensing to produce annual maps of coffee distribution from 2016 to 2024. We analyzed the spatial patterns of annual coffee distribution during this period, and evaluated the potential implications of EUDR for coffee production in Indonesia. Our maps of coffee agroecosystems demonstrate an overall classification accuracy exceeding 80%, and are broadly consistent with independent coffee datasets (i.e. national statistics and coffee probability maps from the Forest Data Partnership). We detected a net increase of ∼16% in coffee area over the eight-year period, although the patterns of change vary across provinces. Based on these findings, we estimate that 87.9% of the mapped coffee area in 2024 meets the EUDR deforestation-free criterion, and only a relatively small proportion of agroecosystems are classified as non-deforestation-free. These findings highlight opportunities for spatially targeted EUDR implementation, where deforestation-free coffee agroecosystems can be supported towards meeting broader EUDR requirements, while areas associated with forest conversion can be supported towards other pathways, such as sustainable agricultural practices, restoration, and forest conservation.

explanation: 该论文研究了亚马逊雨林夜间边界层（NBL）的观测复杂动力学和CO2传输，使用了CloudRoots-Amazon22观测数据，并与理想化模型进行了对比。这涉及到大气环境遥感和空气成分分析，因此与题目要求的相关性较高。
authors: Anna C. Huitema;Vincent S. de Feiter;Raquel González-Armas;Oscar K. Hartogensis;Hella van Asperen;Cleo Q. Dias-Júnior;Jordi Vilà-Guerau de Arellano
title: From prototypical regimes to observed complex dynamics and CO2 transport in the Amazonian nocturnal boundary layer
abstract:
We studied how well idealised models of the nighttime boundary layer capture observed variability above the Amazon rainforest, using observations from the CloudRoots-Amazon22 campaign. The observations indicate large nocturnal variability, caused by non-stationary processes and interactions between the within- and above-canopy atmosphere. Common weather and climate models often miss this variability, highlighting the need to represent the complex forest-atmosphere interactions better. 
 We investigated the characteristics of the nocturnal boundary layer (NBL) above and within the Amazon rainforest canopy during the 2022 dry season. We analysed observed NBL dynamics and CO2 transport from the perspective of the prototypical NBL represented in weather and climate models. To this end, using the CloudRoots-Amazon22 dataset, we characterised the main NBL features and governing processes. We identified NBL height using five methods based on thermal stratification, wind, and turbulent criteria, finding a distinct stable layer above the canopy with an average height between 142–164 m. To examine the drivers of the dynamic NBL evolution, we classified the data into weakly and strongly stable regimes, determined by the interplay between stabilising longwave radiative cooling and destabilising mechanical wind shear. Budget equations for turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), heat, and CO2 allowed us to quantify the relative contributions of these drivers to transport across the canopy-atmosphere interface. In the weakly stable regime, increased TKE at the canopy top promoted mixing between the within- and above-canopy layers. Conversely, TKE was nearly absent in the strongly stable regime, decoupling the two layers. This decoupling favoured strong thermal stratification above the canopy and well-mixed conditions within the canopy. Our results show that only about 6 % of observed profiles conform to prototypical NBL regimes, emphasising the need to revisit parameterisations to explicitly account for canopy-induced effects and intermittent turbulence. Our observational analysis provides a critical benchmark for improving the representation of NBL dynamics and CO2 transport in models.

explanation: 该论文研究了利用氡（radon）来改进甲烷（methane）排放估计的方法，通过双重示踪剂反演（dual-tracer inversion）技术，旨在提高甲烷通量估计的可靠性。这涉及到大气传输模型和温室气体排放估计，与大气环境遥感技术（如大气成分分析、排放监测）密切相关，因此该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Fabian Maier;Christian Rödenbeck;Ute Karstens;Frank-Thomas Koch;Maksym Gachkivskyi;Andrew Smerald;Christoph Gerbig
title: Can radon help to improve methane emission estimates? Results from a dual-tracer inversion
abstract:
Transport model errors represent a major source of uncertainty in greenhouse gas flux estimates derived from inverse modelling, yet they remain challenging to quantify. In our study, we leverage the similarities in the atmospheric transport of methane (CH4) and radon (222Rn) by performing a dual-tracer CH4-222Rn inversion over Europe, with the goal of enhancing the reliability of CH4 flux estimates. We discuss the benefits and limitations of this dual-tracer approach. 
 A major source of uncertainty in inverse modelling of greenhouse gas emissions are deficits in atmospheric transport models, in particular in the description of vertical mixing within the planetary boundary layer (PBL). The properties of radon-222 (Rn) makes it a suitable natural tracer for vertical mixing in the PBL. When comparing the CH4 model-data mismatch (MDM), i.e. the differences between the observed and modelled CH4 concentrations, with the MDM of Rn, we found substantial correlations for several observation sites in central Europe in 2021 (the median CH4-Rn MDM correlation coefficient is 0.6), indicating that a large part of the CH4 and Rn MDM variability can be explained by common errors in the simulated (vertical) transport. We aim to exploit this information in a joint inversion for CH4 and Rn by taking into account prior uncertainties and making use of the fact that the transport model error is correlated between the two gases. We use simultaneous CH4 and Rn observations from 17 sites across central Europe in 2021. The dual-tracer CH4-Rn inversion yields lower CH4 fluxes in several countries covered by the observation sites compared to a single-tracer CH4-only inversion without Rn information. The differences in country-total CH4 fluxes between the dual-tracer and single-tracer inversions are on the order of a few percent and depend on the assumed uncertainty for the Rn prior fluxes. These findings underscore the importance of accurate Rn flux maps for fully leveraging the dual-tracer approach and enhancing the reliability of CH4 flux estimates.

explanation: 该论文研究从实测数据中推导积云云底的饱和水汽过饱和度，属于大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析范畴，涉及云物理和热力学过程，与空气质量监测和卫星观测相关。
topic_words: ['water vapor supersaturation', 'cumulus cloud base', 'in situ measurements', 'atmospheric thermodynamics']
authors: Ramon C. Braga;Manfred Wendisch;Rachel Albrecht;Daniel Harrison
title: A new method to derive water vapor supersaturation at cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements
abstract:
We introduce a new thermodynamic framework to derive water vapor supersaturation at warm cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements. The framework describes the local transition between saturated thermodynamic states as an adiabatic and reversible process under quasi-isobaric conditions, in which the latent energy released during condensation is partitioned between changes in internal energy and water-vapor expansion work. 
 Current in situ measurements of water vapor supersaturation (Sv) with respect to liquid water at cloud base are highly uncertain due to instrumental limitations. Consequently, Sv is commonly estimated using cloud microphysical models and parameterizations. Here, we derive Sv at warm cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements through calculations of the energy and water vapor budgets associated with cloud formation. The derived Sv provides a thermodynamic analogue to the supersaturation established in a cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) chamber, enabling direct comparison with independently measured CCN activation spectra below cloud base. To this end, we formulate the energy budget of a saturated rising air parcel at cloud base and treat the transition between saturated thermodynamic states locally as quasi-isobaric. Under these conditions, the latent heat (Q) released during condensational droplet growth is determined by the corresponding sensible enthalpy difference between the saturated-vapor and water vapor–liquid states. According to the first law of thermodynamics, Q is partitioned between the change in internal energy (ΔU) and water vapor expansion work (Ws). Within this diagnostic framework, part of the condensational energy is, therefore, spent on Ws, reducing the amount of liquid water formed relative to the limiting case in which the entire condensational energy contributes to droplet growth. Accordingly, the cloud supersaturation (Sc) is diagnostically partitioned into liquid-phase (Sl) and vapor-phase (Sv) components based on the fractions of Q associated with ΔU and Ws, respectively. This framework enables the derivation of Sv from airborne cloud-base measurements through thermodynamic constraints on condensational energy partitioning. Here we use airborne measurements collected in growing convective cumuli over the Amazon Basin during the ACRIDICON-CHUVA campaign. Our results demonstrate that the derived cloud droplet number concentration as a function of Sv agrees, within measurement uncertainties, with Sv activation spectra of CCN measured below cloud base.

explanation: 该研究关注苯和苯酚等芳香族化合物在大气中的二次有机气溶胶形成机制，涉及大气化学动力学、空气质量模型和气溶胶演化等关键内容，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和气溶胶分析密切相关。
authors: Aurélien Le Bayon;Aliisa Ojala;Siddharth Iyer;Zhizhao Wang;Victor Lannuque;Florian Couvidat;Raluca Ciuraru;Karine Sartelet
title: Molecular representation of benzene and phenol secondary organic aerosols
abstract:
Aromatics compounds emitted in the atmosphere, such as benzene and phenol, contribute to the formation of organic aerosols. This study presents and evaluates an updated description of benzene chemistry, in which the most influential pathways are identified, including one developed in this work. The resulting mechanism reproduces laboratory observation with great accuracy and is reduced for use in large-scale air quality models. 
 Recent experimental and theoretical work has highlighted missing pathways in the oxidation of aromatic compounds, with consequences for the formation of highly oxygenated products relevant to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. In this study we develop an updated, quasi-explicit oxidation mechanism for benzene based on Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM) v3.3.1, extended to represent key multi-generation chemistry. Quantum chemical calculations are used to derive the formation and evolution of geminal-diol bicyclic peroxy radicals and to parameterize the subsequent molecular rearrangements. The mechanism further incorporates autoxidation sequences previously developed for peroxy and alkoxy radicals, successive OH additions and cyclic epoxides formation. This approach enables a more mechanistic description of aromatic oxidation leading to highly oxygenated, low-volatility products. The mechanism is evaluated using box-model simulations against a set of chamber experiments conducted under various conditions. Simulated aerosol concentrations agree well with observations and emphasize the dominant contribution of the newly implemented pathways. The quasi-explicit mechanism is subsequently reduced using the GENerator of reduced Organic Aerosol mechanisms (GENOA), resulting in a semi-explicit mechanism reduced to 1 % of its original number of species while reproducing SOA mass with a mean error of 3.9 % relative to the quasi-explicit scheme. Using the validated reduced mechanism, zero-dimensional simulations under contrasted atmospheric conditions are conducted to estimate the SOA compounds that are formed in the early stages of oxidation and those that dominate the system at later stages.

authors: Xiaojie Li;Jinming Ge;Yucheng Qiu;Qiaoyi Lv;Wei Song;Jie Zhang;Chi Zhang;Bochun Liu;Jiapeng Wang;Hongwei Xia;Yuhang Zhu
title: Physically constrained retrieval of fog visibility from millimeter-wavelength cloud radar observations
abstract:
Fog threatens transportation but is hard to monitor. Ground sensors see only single points and satellites miss vertical detail. We developed a radar-based method to estimate visibility inside fog based on how fog droplets block light. The method finds water content and droplet sizes from radar signals, then calculates how far one can see. It provides three-dimensional fog monitoring without extra instruments. 
 Fog severely degrades visibility (Vis) and poses substantial risks to transportation and aviation, yet quantitative monitoring remains challenging because conventional ground-based instruments provide spatially limited point observations and cannot resolve three-dimensional fog structure, while passive satellite retrievals have insufficient vertical resolution and difficulty separating fog from low cloud. Millimeter-wavelength cloud radar (MMCR) can penetrate fog and provide fine spatiotemporal resolution, but many radar Vis retrievals rely on empirical reflectivity–visibility relations. This study develops a physically constrained, observation-calibrated single-wavelength Ka-band MMCR retrieval that links reflectivity, liquid water content (LWC), geometric median radius, extinction, and Vis through lognormal droplet-size-distribution moments. A segment-wise mass-absorption LWC power law and an extinction-oriented radius power law are fitted to same-source FM-120 extinction-matching pseudo-targets, achieving a mean absolute fractional extinction error of 9.37 % on the development dataset. In ten spring-2025 DNQ3-conditioned cases, the present retrieval attains a mean absolute error of 0.092 km, while the local FM-120 and Liu et al. (2019) relations yield broadly comparable ranges and the Gultepe et al. (2009) relation departs more strongly. This method improves the physical self-consistency of single-band MMCR fog Vis retrieval without requiring auxiliary in-situ observations and provides technical support for three-dimensional coastal fog monitoring and traffic meteorological early warning.

explanation: 该论文研究了EUMETSAT的Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager（MTG-LI）的性能，这是一个用于监测闪电活动的地球静止轨道光学位移系统。闪电是大气化学和气象学的重要指标，因此该研究直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是与闪电监测和大气成分分析相关。
topic_words: ['Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager', 'lightning detection', 'geostationary lightning location system', 'atmospheric chemistry']
authors: Bartolomeo Viticchié;Sven-Erik Enno;David Navia;Janja Avbelj;Jochen Grandell
title: Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager detection performances
abstract:
Lightning is a vital meteorological indicator, an Essential Climate Variable, and a key factor in atmospheric chemistry. EUMETSAT’s Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager (MTG-LI), operational since July 2024, is Europe’s first space-based geostationary lightning location system devoted to lightning diagnosis and characterization. This manuscript assesses its performance over 18 months, serving as a foundational reference for users. 
 The EUMETSAT Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager (MTG-LI) is the European space-based geostationary lightning location system devoted to the diagnosis and characterization of lightning activity over hemispheric scale. In this publication, we present the assessment of MTG-LI detection performances against four different reference systems: the Vaisala Global Lightning Detection Network (GLD360), the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID), and Geostationary Lightning Mappers (GLMs) −16 and −19 aboard NOAA GOES satellites. The analysis period is eighteen months: from July 2024 to December 2025. MTG-LI absolute flash detection efficiency varies between 70 % (day) and 95 % (night), with an average value of 87.4 %. Its average flash  false  alarm  rate  is  generally below 0.5 flash s−1, while the average fraction of false flashes is 0.16 % of the total flashes. Finally, both average timing and location accuracy are presented and discussed.

explanation: 该论文研究的是一种拉格朗日粒子追踪框架，用于模拟云中粒子的生长和合并，涉及大气微物理过程，这是大气环境遥感技术中的一个重要研究方向。虽然论文没有直接提到空气质量监测或卫星观测，但其对粒子追踪和模拟的研究与大气成分分析、气溶胶检索等领域密切相关。
topic_words: ['Lagrangian particle tracking', 'cloud particles', 'super-droplet simulations', 'atmospheric microphysics', 'particle-based models']
authors: Chongzhi Yin;Shin-Ichiro Shima;Chunsong Lu
title: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the  super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1:  implementation and computational evaluation
abstract:
We developed and tested a way to trace selected cloud particles in a simulation, including how they grow and merge. One run identifies particles that meet chosen conditions, and a second reconstructs only their saved histories. In a three-dimensional test, the saved data were estimated to be one-fifth of what would be needed to keep all particle histories. Larger reductions are possible when fewer particles are selected, making such studies more practical in large simulations. 
 Lagrangian particle histories provide a useful way to diagnose cloud-microphysical pathways in particle-based models, but their practical use in massively parallel super-droplet simulations depends on how particle identifiers, event records, output files, and post-processing workflows are implemented. This paper documents and evaluates a Lagrangian particle-tracking framework in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1. The framework includes forward tracking, backward tracking, and Two-Pass Hybrid Tracking (TPHT). Forward tracking saves the later states of super-droplets selected before or during a simulation. Backward tracking saves the rank and record location of each selected super-droplet's predecessor at the previous output time, so that post-processing can retrieve that record with an 𝒪(1) lookup instead of searching all super-droplets. Both methods use a common procedure to select all valid super-droplets, a random or height–radius-stratified sample, or an externally supplied target list. TPHT uses two integrations over the same physical time interval. The first records super-droplet identifiers when a chosen radius or coalescence condition is met. After duplicate identifiers are removed, the second starts from the same physical and random-number state and writes backward links only for this reduced set. Controlled computational tests are used to characterise runtime, peak random-access memory (RAM), storage (disk-output volume), the effect of output interval on file volume and mean write time, and sampling error and seed-to-seed variability. A three-dimensional DYCOMS-II RF02 stratocumulus case demonstrates TPHT. In this demonstration, the target criteria selected 19.3 % of the estimated valid super-droplet identities, corresponding to an estimated 5.2-fold reduction in retained backward output after temporary identifier files were removed. This factor is specific to the broad criteria used in this test; much larger reductions are possible for problems with sparser target populations. Agreement of the recorded coalescence events between the two integrations provided evidence of reproducibility under the tested configuration. The case study shows that TPHT can identify particles of interest and reconstruct their saved histories while reducing retained output. In future, the same approach could be applied to other history- or event-based questions, including entrainment and mixing, sedimentation, and ice-particle growth.

topic_words: ['Atmospheric Rivers', 'Baroclinic Annular Mode', 'precipitation extremes', 'atmospheric moisture transport']
authors: Sandro W. Lubis;L. Ruby Leung;J. Michael Battalio
title: More Frequent Atmospheric Rivers and Associated Precipitation Extremes Induced by the Baroclinic Annular Mode
abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) play a crucial role in the global hydrological cycle, yet how the intrinsic midlatitude atmospheric variability modulates their activity on subseasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AR frequency and landfall in both hemispheres vary strongly with the strength and phase of the Baroclinic Annular Mode (BAM). During its positive phase, BAM increases AR occurrence by up to ∼50% and AR‐driven precipitation extremes by up to ∼40% relative to climatology. Stronger and more frequent ARs during the positive phase of the BAM are primarily driven by enhanced potential‐to‐kinetic energy conversion, which favors AR growth and intensification, particularly in the storm‐track regions. This response is consistent with dynamically enhanced poleward moisture transport due to a more baroclinically unstable and stormier environment. The results underscore the importance of BAM‐related intrinsic midlatitude storm‐track variability in modulating global AR activity and its potential to improve extended‐range AR prediction on subseasonal timescales.

authors: Zhenwei Liu;Chuan Huang;Jinru Cheng;Tangsheng Cheng;Hang Zhou;Chaomei Wu;Chen Liang;Tingdi Chen;Weilong Luo;Chong Wang;Zhaofeng Wang;Ruocan Zhao;Xianghui Xue
title: Seasonal and Diurnal Variability of Thermospheric Metastable Helium Observed by Multi‐Platform Observations and Numerical Modeling
abstract: Metastable helium (He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$) in the thermosphere emits at 1,083 nm and provides a powerful diagnostic of thermospheric composition, solar radiation, and transport. Its detection remains challenging because of its extremely low density and high‐altitude. Here, we present the first multi‐platform study of thermospheric He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ variability using a He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ density model, ground‐based LiDAR observations over Danzhou, China, and SPHEREx 1,083 nm measurements from May 2025 to April 2026. The three data sets show consistent seasonal variability, with reduced He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$‐related signals from late spring to midsummer and enhanced values in autumn and winter. Model results associate this pattern with changes in background ground‐state helium reservoir. A representative diurnal case shows the strongest response at 500–700 km, with enhanced values after 04:50 local time. An additional LiDAR‐observed layer above approximately 950 km is not fully captured by the model, highlighting the need for further He∗ ${\text{He}}^{\ast }$ model development. These results provide observational guidance for helium models.

authors: Thomas Oberleitner;Artem Baklanov;Thiago Berton Ferreira;Gerrit Hoogenboom;Jonas Jägermeyr;Atul K. Jain;Tzu‐Shun Lin;Oleksandr Mialyk;Christoph Müller;Alex C. Ruane;Florian Zabel;Juraj Balkovič;Chenzhi Wang;Babacar Faye;Jose R. Guarin;Toshichika Iizumi;Nikolay Khabarov;Wenfeng Liu;Masashi Okada;Sam S. Rabin;Clemens Scheer;Rastislav Skalský;Christian Folberth
title: Explaining Climatic Drivers of Yield Anomalies in Global Crop Models Through Metamodel‐Based Attribution
abstract: Global gridded crop models (GGCMs) are important tools for assessing climate impacts on agriculture, yet significant divergence in their projections limits interpretability, and impact studies often treat GGCMs as black boxes. Targeted ensemble sensitivity analyses are demanding and not transferable to different ensembles. Here, we comprehensively evaluate climatic and soil drivers of crop yield anomalies in a state‐of‐the‐art GGCM ensemble, using maize as a representative crop. Gradient boosting classifiers detect anomalies, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values quantify feature importance, and methods are applied to a recent GGCM experiment driven by reanalysis climate data. We find broadly similar climatic drivers across the ensemble, though feature importance distributions differ. Low precipitation dominates under rainfed conditions, while solar radiation typically ranks second, highlighting that drought impacts depend on atmospheric water demand often omitted from sensitivity analyses. In some GGCMs, excess rather than insufficient water drives anomalies. The comparison with climate sensitivities derived from a global yield reference data set indicates that no single GGCM performs best across all climate regions. Individual GGCMs may respond well to one climatic stressor but not others, underscoring that bulk benchmarking of GGCMs against observations can obfuscate processes requiring targeted improvement. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating opportunistic data, that is, experiments produced for other purposes, yields vital insights into GGCM divergence in impact studies. Code is publicly available on GitHub to support future attribution analyses and inform broad audiences about drivers of observed results.

authors: Anyifang Zhang;Ziheng Zhu;Qin Jiang;Quan Yuan;Kaiyue Shan
title: Intensifying Tropical Cyclones and Expanding Renewable Energy Call for Climate‐Resilient Planning in China
abstract: Variable renewable energy (VRE) is central to power system decarbonization for climate mitigation, yet its rapid expansion places growing VRE infrastructure at risk from tropical cyclones (TCs). With TCs projected to intensify, such risks remain poorly quantified at policy‐relevant scales, potentially exposing power systems to unforeseen disruption and damage. Here, we develop a spatially resolved risk projection model by coupling a physics‐based TC hazard module with a power system optimization module to assess the impact of TC climatology change on VRE expansion in China. We find that the TC‐induced economic losses to VRE are projected to increase 10‐ to 20‐fold relative to a historical baseline (1975–2014) of 0.37 billion USD yr−1 by the late 21st century (2061–2100), with wind power accounting for 87%–91% of this increase. The decomposition analysis shows that exposure dominates (contributing 44%–49%) the increase in economic loss growth over 2021–2060, whereas hazard‐exposure interaction dominates (contributing 49%–67%) over 2061–2100. We further identify the optimal strengthening metric, which can offset 54%–67% of the projected economic losses. This framework shifts disaster‐risk assessment from reactive recovery to proactive infrastructure resilience planning, providing a scalable template for climate‐resilient coastal energy transitions worldwide.

authors: Jan Swierczek-Jereczek;Javier Blasco;Alexander Robinson;Jorge Alvarez-Solas;Marisa Montoya
title: Antarctic marine-based ice destabilized when warming outpaces solid-Earth feedbacks
abstract:
Delayed bedrock uplift can allow rapid warming to trigger Antarctic Ice Sheet retreat before classical instability thresholds are reached, lowering critical warming thresholds by up to 0.5 K in East Antarctica, according to coupled model simulations. 
 The Antarctic Ice Sheet is expected to be the largest contributor to sea-level rise over the coming centuries. Previous equilibrium ice-sheet simulations have suggested that this is due to crossing a bifurcation point associated with marine ice-sheet instability. Here we investigate whether sectors vulnerable to this instability can undergo rate-induced tipping, whereby rapid forcing and slow bedrock uplift trigger self-sustained retreat before the bifurcation point is reached. We test this with an ice-sheet model coupled to a glacial isostatic adjustment model, sampling the uncertainty in mantle viscosity. We find that slow bedrock adjustment weakens the stabilizing effect of glacial isostatic adjustment, allowing grounding lines to reach retrograde bed slopes more readily and triggering self-sustained retreat below the bifurcation threshold. Although the West Antarctic Ice Sheet is subject to a bifurcation, it is unlikely to experience rate-induced tipping because of the low mantle viscosity beneath the region. In contrast, the Recovery and Aurora subglacial basins are likely to undergo such a transition even under warming rates lower than those observed today. Depending on mantle viscosity, this mechanism can reduce the critical global mean temperature anomaly by up to 0.5 K, with important implications for the long-term evolution of the Earth system. Delayed bedrock uplift can allow rapid warming to trigger Antarctic Ice Sheet retreat before classical instability thresholds are reached, lowering critical warming thresholds by up to 0.5 K in East Antarctica, according to coupled model simulations.

explanation: 该研究涉及X射线自由电子激光(XFEL)与物质之间的非线性相互作用，产生的太赫兹发射可用于探测固态材料的二阶X射线非线性和超快极化动力学，这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和大气成分分析等方向密切相关，因此具有相关性。
authors: N. Kida;T. Togashi;K. Tono;Y. Ikemoto;K. Sawada
title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
abstract:
The authors show that hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses generate terahertz emission in ZnTe through X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG). The findings establish a route to probing second-order X-ray nonlinearity and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids. 
 Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids. The authors show that hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses generate terahertz emission in ZnTe through X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG). The findings establish a route to probing second-order X-ray nonlinearity and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

explanation: 该论文研究了南印度辐合带（SICC）在温室效应下的变化，特别是其向南摆动的频率和强度增加，这直接关系到气候变化对天气模式的影响，进而影响空气质量监测（如极端降雨和洪水）。虽然论文没有明确提到遥感技术，但其研究内容与大气环境遥感密切相关，因为气候变化和天气模式的改变是大气环境监测的重要领域。
authors: Haodong Wang;Tao Geng;Wenju Cai;Xiaopei Lin
title: Increased southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone under greenhouse warming
abstract:
Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can lead to severe rainfall and flooding in southern Africa. Here the authors show that climate change leads to an increase in the frequency and intensity of such swings. 
 Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can induce devastating floods over parts of southern Africa. How greenhouse warming affects such southward swings is not well understood. Here we show that, under a high-emissions scenario, the frequency of extreme southward swings doubles from one event per 22 years in the twentieth century to one per 10 years in the twenty-first century with an average increase in rainfall intensity of 20%. The increased frequency is related to faster warming of the African continent than of the Indian Ocean that intensifies northerly winds, and to a poleward migration of Southern Ocean westerlies that drives a pattern of faster subtropical Indian Ocean warming to the south and enhances Atlantic-to-Africa moisture transport, both of which favour a southward swing of the South Indian convergence zone. More frequent southward migration of the South Indian convergence zone might thus indicate increasing flooding risk in parts of southern Africa. Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can lead to severe rainfall and flooding in southern Africa. Here the authors show that climate change leads to an increase in the frequency and intensity of such swings.

explanation: 该论文研究的是Da Qi-1 ACDL卫星对XCO2（二氧化碳柱平均干空气摩尔分数）的遥感测量，并与被动卫星（如OCO-2、OCO-3、GOSAT）的产品一致性进行比较，这直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，特别是大气成分分析和卫星观测。
authors: Yike Wang;Ge Han;Hongyuan Zhang;Yiyang Huang;Kangjie Zhou;Wei Gong
title: Assessing the consistency of XCO2 products from DQ-1 ACDL and passive satellites using a unified comparison framework
abstract:
This study establishes a unified framework to assess the consistency of DQ-1 (Da Qi-1) ACDL (Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar) XCO2 with passive satellite products while considering sampling and column-definition differences. DQ-1 agrees well with TCCON (Total Carbon Column Observing Network) and shows consistent spatial patterns with OCO-2, OCO-3 (Orbiting Carbon Observatory), GOSAT, and GOSAT-2 (Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite) over selected regions. It provides complementary XCO2 observations where passive measurements are limited, including nighttime and high latitudes, supporting future joint carbon monitoring and inversion studies. 
 Da Qi-1 (DQ-1) carries the Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar (ACDL), a spaceborne integrated path differential absorption (IPDA) lidar that retrieves the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide (XCO2)  using active laser measurements. Unlike passive near-infrared/shortwave-infrared sensors that rely on reflected sunlight, ACDL can observe at night and high latitudes, but its sampling and effective column definition differ from passive XCO2 products. Evaluation is therefore needed before active and passive observations can be interpreted jointly. We compare DQ-1 ACDL with the Orbiting Carbon Observatory (OCO-2 and OCO-3) and Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite (GOSAT and GOSAT-2) missions from June 2022–December 2024 using a unified framework that combines Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS)-based coherence assessment, sampling availability, daily 2° aggregation, spatiotemporal collocation, and correction for XCO2 column-definition differences. Validation against the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) gives R=0.92, a mean bias of 0.21 ppm, and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.49 ppm for daytime DQ-1, comparable to GOSAT. Over coherent and well-sampled regions, DQ-1 is broadly consistent with OCO-2 and OCO-3, with mean differences generally below 0.5 ppm and similar spatial and meridional structures. Over ocean, the DQ-1–OCO differences vary with surface reflectance and wind speed, with different reflectance relationships for OCO-2 and OCO-3. Nighttime DQ-1 is also broadly consistent with CAMS-derived XCO2. Regional analyses show complementary DQ-1 coverage where passive observations are limited. These results support DQ-1 ACDL as a quantitatively comparable and complementary component of the satellite XCO2 observing system.

explanation: 该论文研究了GHGSat卫星星座对甲烷泄漏的探测和量化性能，涉及卫星遥感技术、大气成分分析和空气质量监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Antoine Ramier;Hanford Deglint;Ariane Deslieres;Lia Formenti;Marianne Girard;Dylan Jervis;David J. Marshall;Jean-Philippe W. MacLean;Jason McKeever;Andrew McKell;Mathias Strupler;Ewan Tarrant
title: Performance validation of the GHGSat methane constellation via controlled releases
abstract:
We validated the GHGSat fleet against a large set of precisely measured emissions from 2021 to 2026 and built a model linking detection probability to leak rate, wind, retrieval noise, and resolution. In typical conditions the satellites detect a leak of about 100 kilograms per hour half the time and quantify its rate accurately. This sets a clear benchmark for how reliably satellites detect and measure methane leaks, which is essential for trustworthy emissions reporting and mitigation. 
 Satellite remote sensing has become an important tool for detecting, quantifying, and attributing methane emissions, yet a rigorous, condition-dependent characterization of point-source imager performance validated against controlled releases with known emission rates remains limited, despite being essential to support its use in regulatory and voluntary reporting frameworks. We present a comprehensive performance assessment of the GHGSat constellation of high-resolution methane-imaging satellites based on a multi-campaign controlled release dataset spanning 2021 to 2026 that combines self-organized campaigns with independent third-party experiments. We develop a probabilistic, environmental conditions-dependent detection model in which the probability of detection depends on the plume signal to noise ratio (SNR), which is in turn a function of emission rate, wind speed, retrieval noise, and spatial resolution. Comparing model variants over subsets of these predictors, we find that emission rate, wind speed, and retrieval noise are the dominant drivers of detection, while spatial resolution improves the fit only when combined with the others. We find that an SNR of 1.72 ± 0.39 is required to achieve a 50 % probability of detection, which translates to a detection limit Q50 = 99.0 ± 5.3 kg h−1 in median environmental conditions encountered in controlled releases (3 m s−1 wind speed, 7 mmol m−2 column density noise, 27 m resolution). Evaluated over global observing conditions, the same model gives a median Q50= 159.7 kg h−1. The estimated Q50 is shown to converge stably as data accumulate and to remain consistent when blind validation samples are added to self-organized releases. Quantification accuracy is evaluated through parity analysis of estimated versus metered emission rates, yielding an ordinary least squares slope of 0.93 ± 0.03 and R2 of 0.92 using reported model winds, improving to 0.98 ± 0.03 and R2= 0.93 with a co-located anemometer wind adjusted to a 10 m reference height. A comparison of emission rate estimates based on ERA5, IFS, and HRRR winds shows that quantification accuracy metrics derived from this dataset were largely insensitive to the choice of operationally available wind product, with a residual underestimation at low emission rates that correlates with wind model spatial resolution. We further demonstrate a bias correction combining a local concentration background correction with an empirically recalibrated effective wind speed, which recovers the low-rate sources that were previously underestimated and removes most of the residual bias without degrading accuracy at higher emission rates. These results establish a transparent, statistically grounded baseline for the GHGSat constellation's detection and quantification performance and provide a methodological framework that can be extended as additional controlled-release data become available.

explanation: 该论文研究的是韩国济州岛降水中的稳定水同位素数据，包括δ18O和δ2H的测量值，以及与气温、降水量的相关性。这些数据可用于分析大气成分和水分循环，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量和大气成分分析相关。
authors: Kwang-Sik Lee;Dong-Chan Koh;Young-Hee Kim;Won-Bae Park;Songyi Kim;Hyejung Jung;Yeon-Sik Bong;Woo-Jin Shin;Chaeyoung Kim;Jeonghoon Lee
title: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
abstract:
We present 462 paired measurements of stable oxygen and hydrogen isotopes in monthly precipitation from 15 sites on Jeju Island, South Korea, collected between 2000 and 2003. Isotope values were generally lower in summer and decreased with elevation. Published with weather data and sampling information, this historical dataset provides a baseline for future monitoring and supports research on groundwater recharge and the island’s water cycle. 
 Spatially resolved, multi-year observations of stable water isotopes in precipitation remain scarce for high-relief maritime islands. We present a historical dataset of monthly precipitation isotopes collected between September 2000 and December 2003 at 15 stations on Jeju Island, South Korea, spanning elevations of 5–1230 ma.s.l. The dataset contains 462 paired δ18O and δ2H measurements, deuterium excess (d-excess = δ2H − 8 × δ18O), station and sampling metadata, and 488 station-month records of precipitation and air-temperature estimates, including 26 records without corresponding isotope measurements. Missing isotope observations were not imputed. Individual δ18O and δ2H values range from −13.2 ‰ to −2.0 ‰ and from −93.3 ‰ to −5.8 ‰, respectively, and generally exhibit lower values in summer than during the cool season. Unweighted station means for the common 2002–2003 period yield elevation gradients of −0.146 ± 0.013 ‰ per 100 m for δ18O and −1.043 ± 0.128 ‰ per 100 m for δ2H, with uncertainties expressed as standard errors. An island–nearshore comparison with isotope-enabled model output provides context for broad seasonal variability. By recovering and openly publishing observations collected more than two decades ago, this dataset preserves a historical baseline for subsequent precipitation-isotope monitoring and hydrological studies on Jeju Island. The data are available at https://doi.org/10.22747/paper_data.20260219.42 (Lee et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及野火事件的数据库构建，野火是大气环境中的一个重要因素，其监测和研究对于空气质量、大气成分分析等具有重要意义。
authors: Eric S. Kasischke;Nancy H. French
title: An integrated wildfire event database for improved fire science research for the continental United States, 1992–2021
abstract:
A new wildfire event dataset was developed to improve information for studying wildfires in the continental United State for 1992 to 2021. It was created by integrating data from three existing datasets with information obtained from regional reports and datasets and reports found on the world wide web. For all United States regions, calculations using this new dataset increases total burned area, as well as the number of and burned  area in extreme wildfires (those larger than 5000 hectares). 
 This paper describes a wildfire event dataset that was initially created by mining information from three existing national datasets that have provided the foundation for numerous wildfire studies in the continental United States over the past two decades. The goal for creating this dataset was to address existing uncertainties and ambiguities in the the existing datasets by using information from regional reports and datasets and searches of the world wide web. Wildfire events not contained in the three datasets were added as new records. Approaches were developed to harvest information for records where there were significant differences in the size of the same fire from different datasets. Specific attention was paid to fires named as complexes, those contained multiple fires, smaller events that had merged to form larger events, events that had joined, events where the size was incorrectly reported, and duplicate events. This new wildfire event dataset provides more accurate information on the number and sizes of individual wildfires and improved information for quantifying annual area burned and changes in extreme wildfire activity over a three-decade period (1992 to 2021) at different spatial scales. Results are presented that illustrate the differences in wildfire characteristics developed from the new dataset and those currently being used by the fire science community.

explanation: 该论文使用多传感器卫星观测数据（如MODIS、VIIRS和OLCI）开发了一个关于中国边缘海域漂浮大型藻类（如Ulva prolifera和Sargassum horneri）的周度数据集，涉及了藻华的监测、季节性模式、年际变化和快速动态，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析等领域密切相关。
authors: Mingqing Liu;Zhaotong Chen;Yingcheng Lu;Qianguo Xing;Jiaochan Hu;Haoyang Yu;Zhongbin B. Li;Mengqiu Wang
title: A 1-km weekly dataset of floating Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri blooms in China’s marginal seas derived from multi-sensor satellite observations
abstract:
Floating macroalgal blooms in China’s coastal seas can rapidly expand and spread, affecting marine ecosystems and human activities. This study developed a weekly dataset of two major floating macroalgae species from 2018 to 2025 using observations from multiple satellites. The dataset captures seasonal patterns, yearly changes, and rapid bloom dynamics, providing a consistent resource for understanding bloom development and supporting coastal monitoring. 
 Floating macroalgae blooms, primarily caused by Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri, frequently occur in the marginal seas around China, posing significant ecological and economic challenges.  However, a long-term, high-frequency monitoring dataset capable of capturing bloom seasonality, interannual variability, and rapid transport dynamics across multiple sea regions remains limited.  In this study, we derived 1-km weekly mean U. prolifera and S. horneri dataset covering 2018 to 2025, generated from 85,868 multi-sensor satellite images acquired from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), and Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI).  By integrating complementary observations from multiple satellite sensors, the dataset substantially improves temporal continuity and observation availability relative to single-sensor products, enabling more complete characterization of rapidly evolving macroalgal blooms.  A two-step deep learning-based approach was employed to detect and distinguish U. prolifera and S. horneri, achieving >90% accuracy for both bloom extraction and species classification across sensors.  Independent validation using hyperspectral Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) Ocean Color Instrument (OCI) and Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) data further supports the reliability of species discrimination.  The pair-wise cross-sensor biomass comparisons show strong consistency, with R² > 0.8 for both species.  The dataset reveals distinct spatiotemporal patterns of the two macroalgal species.  U. prolifera blooms in the Yellow Sea exhibit a relatively consistent seasonal cycle from May to August, with rapid aggregation and dissipation and the highest biomass recorded in 2021, whereas S. horneri shows a broader and more variable distribution across the East China Sea, with record-high biomass observed in 2024.  Weekly observations further resolve rapid bloom aggregation, transport, and dissipation processes that are difficult to capture using monthly composites.  Weekly products provide a balance between temporal resolution and observational completeness, preserving short-term bloom variability while supporting consistent interannual comparisons.  Compared with weekly products, monthly composites underestimated seasonal peak biomass by 24–50% for S. horneri and 12–52% for U. prolifera during 2018–2025.  In contrast, daily products were more sensitive to short-term biomass fluctuations, which could alter the identification of the year with the highest boom intensity, highlighting the importance of temporal aggregation for robust interannual comparisons.  Comparisons with previous studies and reported bloom events demonstrate that the dataset reliably reproduces observed spatial distributions and seasonal characteristics.  By providing a high-resolution, weekly, and species-resolved dataset of floating macroalgae, this study offers a consistent observational foundation for investigating species-specific bloom dynamics, assessing their responses to environmental variability, and enabling data-driven management and early warning of macroalgal blooms in China’s marginal seas.

explanation: 该论文研究的是多频段卫星土壤湿度数据的协同同化方案，涉及卫星观测、数据融合和同化技术，与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Xuesong Bai;Zhaohui Lin;Zhengkun Qin;Juan Li
title: A preliminary study on a synergistic assimilation scheme for multi-band satellite soil moisture data
abstract:
Accurate soil moisture data is essential for predicting weather. This study examined how observations from three satellites can be combined to improve land-surface simulations. While each satellite helps, their value changes with vegetation type. Merging these data sources gives a more reliable estimate of soil wetness, especially in central and western China. This approach strengthens soil-water monitoring and supports more dependable climate forecasting. 
 Soil moisture retrievals from satellite sensors operating at different microwave frequencies provide diverse and complementary data sources for assimilation. However, fully exploiting the advantages of each frequency band while increasing the volume of assimilated observations remains a challenge. This study assimilates soil-moisture retrievals from three dominant-frequency instruments – SMAP (Soil Moisture Active–Passive), ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer), and MWRI (Microwave Radiation Imager) – into the Common Land Model (CoLM) via the Simplified Extended Kalman Filter (SEKF). Based on the systematic assessment of the disparate impacts of each single-band product, we propose and test a synergistic multi-satellite assimilation framework that optimally combines the complementary information inherent in the multi-frequency observations. Results show that assimilating soil-moisture retrievals improves the accuracy of the CoLM land-surface model; nevertheless, the effectiveness of each product varies with vegetation type. Analyses of simultaneous multi-source assimilation indicate that retrieval uncertainties associated with frequency-dependent differences in vegetation penetration capability are the dominant factor controlling the effectiveness of joint assimilation. When SMAP and ASCAT products are already ingested, the additional introduction of MWRI data over low-stature vegetation, where vegetation attenuation is relatively weak, provides complementary information and further enhances the joint assimilation performance. Validation against in-situ observations across China demonstrates that the largest improvements occur in the central and western parts of the country: compared with the open-loop simulation, the domain-mean correlation coefficient rises by about 0.25, while the error declines from 0.068 to 0.058 m3 m−3. This indicates that improvements from multi-sensor assimilation stem not only from increased data volume but also from the complementary characteristics of the assimilated products. These findings provide valuable insights into the design of synergistic multi-sensor land data assimilation systems and contribute to improving land surface modeling, as well as weather and climate prediction accuracy.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用化学传输模型（CTMs）和化学气候模型（CCMs）来研究地面臭氧、颗粒物（PM）、氮和硫沉降的长程传输及其影响。这些模型用于分析不同全球区域的污染移动和来源贡献，为改进空气质量政策提供科学依据，这与大气成分分析和空气质量监测直接相关。
authors: Tim Butler;Tabish Ansari;Claudio A. Belis;Elisa Bergas-Masso;Willem van Caspel;Hilde Fagerli;Johannes Flemming;Marta Garcia Vivanco;Paul Griffiths;Douglas S. Hamilton;Coralina Hernandez Trujillo;Lena Höglund-Isaksson;Vincent Huijnen;Johannes W. Kaiser;Gerbrand Koren;Zbigniew Klimont;Florian Lindl;Aura Lupascu;Mariano Mertens;Martijn Schaap;Steven T. Turnock;Oliver Wild;Philipp Weiss;Jacek Kaminski;Rosa Wu;Terry Keating
title: HTAP3-OPNS: ozone, PM, nitrogen and sulphur deposition – multi-model experiments to support the revision of the CLRTAP Gothenburg Protocol
abstract:
Air pollution travels across continents, meaning emissions in one region can affect air quality far away. To better understand this, scientists from many groups are planning to run coordinated computer simulations of the atmosphere. By comparing results across models and emission scenarios, the planned study will show how pollution moves between regions and which sources matter most, helping governments design more effective air quality policies. 
 HTAP3-OPNS is a multi-model exercise designed to support the revision of the Gothenburg Protocol under the UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP). Using an ensemble of Chemical Transport Models (CTMs) and Chemistry-Climate Models (CCMs), this study investigates the long-range transport and impacts of ground-level ozone, particulate matter (PM), and nitrogen and sulphur deposition across different global regions. The project aims to assess the contributions of regional versus extra-regional emission sources, evaluate the suitability of current models, and project changes in air pollution under future emission scenarios and climate conditions. A series of perturbation simulations will enable the development of an ensemble emulator to explore and evaluate potential mitigation strategies efficiently. This paper outlines the scientific and policy questions motivating the study, describes the experimental design, including input datasets, model configurations, and required outputs, and discusses methodologies for data handling and analysis. The results will provide crucial insights for policy decisions aiming to improve air quality, protect human health, and protect ecosystems worldwide.

explanation: 该论文研究雷达和自动气象站（AWS）数据联合同化技术，用于提高重降雨事件的降水预报精度。这涉及大气环境遥感技术，特别是利用雷达和地面观测站数据进行分析，属于空气质量监测和大气成分分析的范畴。
topic_words: ['radar data assimilation', 'automatic weather station (AWS)', 'precipitation forecasts', 'atmospheric instability', 'remote sensing']
authors: Haiqin Chen;Kun Zhao;Xinyu Zhang;Hao Huang;Ang Zhou;Lijian Zhu
title: Combined Assimilation of Radar and AWS Data From Mesoscale Networks for the Record‐Breaking Heavy Rainfall in China
abstract: Radar data assimilation (DA) alone remains insufficient for precipitation forecasts due to the lack of thermodynamic information in the pre‐storm environment. This study investigates the assimilation of dense automatic weather station (AWS) observations from China's mesoscale network alongside radar during an extreme rainfall event caused by the remnant vortex of typhoon Haikui. Optimal sequence and scale representation of dense AWS observations within the operational two‐step DA framework are examined. Results demonstrate that adding regional AWS data to radar and national‐level observations significantly refines surface wind, temperature, and humidity analyses, directly enhancing precipitation forecasts. Notably, assimilating synoptic‐scale information followed by radar outperforms the reverse approach, as initial large‐scale increments stabilize subsequent convective‐scale updates, including stronger maritime airflow, enhanced low‐level convergence and atmospheric instability. Furthermore, despite ∼10 km spacing, AWS data function optimally as synoptic‐scale observations rather than convective‐scale, as the single‐layer temperature and humidity increments with very small decorrelation scales have limited impact in NWP models.

explanation: 该论文研究了气候变化对晴空湍流的影响，晴空湍流是大气环境中的一个重要参数，与航空安全密切相关。论文使用了多个气候模型来分析湍流强度指标的变化，这与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析和空气质量监测有直接关系，因此该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Joana de Medeiros;Paul D. Williams
title: Global Multi‐Model Eddy Dissipation Rate Probability Density Functions for Clear‐Air Turbulence Under Climate Change
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence poses a major risk to aviation, and it is expected to intensify as a response to climate change. The probability density functions (PDFs) of dozens of different clear‐air turbulence (CAT) diagnostics have been found to shift to higher values in response to climate change, consistent with strengthened vertical wind shear at cruising altitudes. The response of the PDF of the eddy dissipation rate (EDR), which is the internationally endorsed measure of turbulence strength, has not previously been studied, however. This study aims to quantify the impacts of these changes in the upper–tropospheric and lower–stratospheric dynamics on global CAT by 2100. By converting 21 CAT diagnostics from multiple climate model simulations into EDR for the historical period of 1950–1980 and the future period of 2070–2100, we find greater probabilities in the right–hand tail of the PDF in the future period compared with the historical period. Multi‐diagnostic‐model metrics show relative increases of 1%–15% in light, 2%–20% in light‐to‐moderate, 3%–20% in moderate, 8%–45% in moderate‐to‐severe, and 10%–50% in severe CAT by the future period depending on scenarios, regions, and seasons. These findings indicate that CAT will become significantly more frequent across all aviation‐relevant intensity levels as the climate continues to change.

explanation: 该论文研究暖季边界层jet在洞庭湖-鄱阳湖区的影响，涉及降水影响、大气组成分析等，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。
authors: Xiaokang Wang;Ming Xue;Yongjie Huang;Cuihong Wu;Xiaofang Wang;Jingyu Wang
title: Characteristics, Mechanisms, and Rainfall Impacts of Warm‐Season Boundary‐Layer Jets in the Dongting‐Poyang Lake Region, South of the Middle Reach of the Yangtze River, China
abstract: Boundary‐layer (BL) jets (BLJs) exhibit significant diurnal variations and can strongly influence precipitation. The Dongting‐Poyang Lake region of China experiences frequent BLJs and heavy rainfall, yet systematic studies remain limited. This study investigates southerly and northeasterly BLJs (SBLJs and NEBLJs) in the region, focusing on their spatiotemporal distributions, formation, and precipitation impacts. SBLJs occur most frequently in summer, characterized by strong, deep south–southwesterly flows with warm advection. SBLJs peak around 02:00 Beijing Time (BJT) and weaken after sunrise as the mixed BL develops, with a typical duration of 1–9 hr. NEBLJs occur mainly in spring and fall, featuring strong but shallow northeasterly flows. NEBLJs peak around 22:00 BJT, show weaker diurnal variability, with a higher proportion of long‐duration cases persisting into daytime. Daily‐mean BLJ winds depend on synoptic patterns, while nocturnal intensification is dominated by BL inertial oscillations. Daytime mixing weakens BL winds, and reduced nighttime friction enables inertial oscillations to strengthen BL flows. Differences in seasons, thermodynamic conditions, and BL depth modulate inertial oscillation phases. This causes NEBLJs to peak ∼4 hr earlier than SBLJs. SBLJ‐associated precipitation concentrates at the jet exit region and peaks during pre‐dawn to early morning. Nocturnal BLJ strengthening enhances moisture flux and convergence to favor rainfall, while daytime deviation winds suppress precipitation. NEBLJ precipitation occurs at the jet exit during pre‐dawn to early morning and on its left side in early evening. Of these, exit‐region rainfall results from moisture transport by BL northerly and overlying southerly, combined with terrain‐induced lift.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国2013年至2020年PM2.5浓度的变化及其对大气年龄的影响，涉及空气质量监测、气象条件和排放变化对大气成分的影响，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Xiaodong Xie;Yang Xiang;Jianlin Hu
title: Responses of the Atmospheric Age of PM2.5 to Changes in Meteorology and Emissions in China From 2013 to 2020
abstract: The clean air actions in China since 2013 have decreased fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations significantly, however, their impacts on the atmospheric age of PM2.5 remain unclear. Here, we updated the age‐resolved Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model to quantify the impacts of changes in anthropogenic emissions and meteorological conditions on the atmospheric age of PM2.5 in China from 2013 to 2020. The results indicated that PM2.5 concentrations decreased by 39.6% in central‐eastern China, primarily driven by anthropogenic emission reductions. The mean atmospheric age of PM2.5 in most of China increased in April and July and decreased in October. In January, the mean age of PM2.5 increased by ∼8.5 hr in the Beijing‐Tianjin‐Hebei region, while it decreased by 5.8–6.7 hr in the Pearl River Delta. Meteorological conditions are the dominant factors influencing PM2.5 age, accounting for 56% in Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei, 39% in the Yangtze River Delta, 56% in the Pearl River Delta, 74% in the Sichuan Basin, and 60% in the Fenwei Plain. Emission reductions increased the atmospheric age of PM2.5 in most of China from 2013 to 2020, with a maximum increase of ∼16 hr during July and April. Our results demonstrate that the best time to start emission control under stable weather conditions needs to be 5–15 hr earlier than that on normal days. With the air quality continuously improving, future short‐term emission controls, especially for large public events, shall be started earlier than before.

explanation: 该研究探讨了平流层极地涡旋与华南地区早中冬季节降水之间的关系，涉及大气环流和降水模式的分析，与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析和降水监测相关。
authors: Guangqi Zhu;Zhexuan Xu;Xu Wang;Ruhua Zhang;Wen Zhou
title: Modulation of the Stratospheric Polar Vortex on the Precipitation Dipole Mode in Southeast China During Early‐to‐Mid Winter
abstract: In this study, we investigated the linkage between the stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) and precipitation in early and mid winter (November–January; NDJ) in Southeast China, using station observations and reanalysis data sets, and verified the linkage using numerical stratospheric nudging model experiments. The results reveal that the SPV has a weak influence on the first empirical orthogonal function (EOF1) mode of precipitation over Southeast China on the interannual timescale, while the second mode (EOF2) characterized by a dipole pattern is related to the strength of SPV with a max 0.49 correlation coefficient. The downward‐propagating SPV signal modulates a Eurasian Rossby wave train characterized by anomalous cyclonic circulation over the Ural sector and anomalous anticyclonic circulation centered near Lake Baikal, corresponding to a weakened Ural ridge and an enhanced Lake Baikal ridge. This circulation configuration alters cold‐air intrusion and contributes to the meridional precipitation dipole over southeastern China. The moisture budget diagnosis shows that this geopotential height anomaly influences the dipole pattern mainly through the vertical dynamic component. Horizontal dynamic and thermodynamic components both exhibit a monopole over southeastern China, however, their effects are opposite. Nudging experiments based on the historical SPV are conducted to disentangle the contribution of the SPV. The stratospheric nudging experiment reproduces parts of the observed circulation and precipitation‐dipole structure. Projection onto the observed EOF2 pattern shows that the ensemble‐reproducible signal accounts for approximately 10% of the simulated PC2 variance, indicating that SPV variability provides a detectable but limited contribution, while atmospheric internal variability remains dominant.

explanation: 该论文研究的是一种特殊的云地闪电（ECS）及其与向下 tera伽马射线闪击（TGF）的关系，使用了闪电定位系统（FALMA）进行数据收集和分析。虽然不直接涉及空气质量监测或卫星遥感技术，但其研究大气放电现象的技术方法和数据分析方法与大气环境遥感技术领域有间接关联，特别是对闪电和大气现象的观测与分析。

title: A Survey of Energetic Compact Strokes in Japan
abstract: Energetic compact strokes (ECSs) are a special type of cloud‐to‐ground (CG) lightning stroke that were found to be consistently associated with downward terrestrial gamma‐ray flashes (TGFs). In this paper, we made a survey of ECSs in a 500‐km‐radius region in Japan using three years of data from the Fast Antenna Lightning Mapping Array (FALMA), a low‐frequency lightning location system. We found that the vast majority of ECSs occur in winter thunderstorms, especially in November and December, along the west coast of Japan. Compared with normal CG strokes, ECSs in winter are more likely to cluster in mountain regions with elevations of a few hundred meters. The tendency of ECSs to cluster in certain regions provides clear guidance for future campaigns to look for downward TGFs, but it also implies the increased possibility of health hazards posed by downward TGFs in these regions. Some ECSs also occur in spring and mostly at high mountain tops. ECSs have a clear tendency to be temporally isolated from other lightning discharges and rarely occur in thunderstorms with high flash rates. Based on these characteristics, we discuss the favorable conditions for the production of ECSs. A comparison with superbolts observed by the World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) shows that out of 10 superbolts observed near Japan, nine are negative CG strokes having similar FALMA waveforms as ECSs. It is possible that a significant fraction of WWLLN superbolts are also ECSs, and we suggest that ECSs can also be commonly found outside of Japan.

title: Cave stalagmites document global patterns in monsoon rainfall over the past 450,000 years
abstract:
A 450,000-year stalagmite record of rainfall in the Amazon Basin , combined with existing Asian records, shows that the global monsoon system has oscillated regularly, strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, during intervals of warmth and warming climate, monsoons in both hemispheres failed for millennia. 
 A 450,000-year stalagmite record of rainfall in the Amazon Basin , combined with existing Asian records, shows that the global monsoon system has oscillated regularly, strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, during intervals of warmth and warming climate, monsoons in both hemispheres failed for millennia. The South American and Asian monsoons have both weakened during past periods of rapid warming.

title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
abstract:
Fifteen years of atmospheric CO2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions. 
 The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1–5, rising tree mortality6–8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9–11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1–4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14–17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011–2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019–2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr−1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning. Fifteen years of atmospheric CO2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions.

title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N2O5 hydrolysis
abstract: Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N2O5hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

authors: Jihai Dong;Wenjin Sun;Baylor Fox-Kemper;Zhiyou Jing;Changming Dong
title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

authors: Ran Du;Xin Wang;Jun Ge;Yanhong Gao
title: Increasing tropical forest fragmentation intensifies extreme high temperatures
abstract: Deforestation, as one of the most pressing global environmental challenges, can intensify local temperature extremes through altering surface properties (e.g. albedo, roughness and evapotranspiration) and the associated land–atmosphere interactions. Prior studies have largely focused on the effects of forest cover changes at the grid scale, whereas the impact of subgrid-scale changes in forest fragmentation has received relatively limited attention. Utilizing satellite-based forest fragmentation index (FFI) data and the ERA5-Land reanalysis data, we investigate impacts of FFI changes in tropical forests on local extreme temperature indices, including the annual mean and maximum values of daily maximum temperature (TXm and TXx, respectively). Our results show that increasing FFI (i.e. forests becoming more fragmented) can significantly intensify extreme temperatures, with each unit increase in FFI corresponding to increases of 0.35 °C –1.14 °C for TXm and 0.83 °C –2.85 °C for TXx. These phenomena are mainly attributed to fragmentation-induced shifts in surface energy partitioning, which reduce latent heat flux and enhance sensible heating. The sensitivities of extreme temperatures to increasing FFI vary by region, with its strength being strongest in the Congo Basin (1.14 °C unit−1 for TXm and 2.85 °C unit−1 for TXx) but weaker in the Amazon basin (0.58 °C unit−1 for TXm and 1.21 °C unit−1 for TXx) and Southeast Asia (0.35 °C unit−1 for TXm and 0.83 °C unit−1 for TXx). These regional differences result from that background hydroclimatic conditions and land–atmosphere coupling strength can modulate the effect of forest fragmentation changes on extreme temperatures. These findings highlight the important role of increasing forest fragmentation in amplification of local temperature extremes, with implications for developing forest management strategies aimed at enhancing resilience to extreme climate events under ongoing warming.

explanation: 该论文研究了半干旱地区 Agrivoltaic (AV) 系统与传统园艺土壤在夏季碳 dioxide efflux 方面的差异。虽然主要关注土壤碳的积累和排放，但其涉及的 CO2 排放测量与大气环境监测技术相关，特别是与空气质量和大气组成分析有关。因此，该论文与遥感技术在环境监测中的应用有较强的关联性。
